name: netdust-devops
description: 0.6.3: three project-local fixes reach the core. Over git-push the payload lives in git, so ship no longer archives nothing and refuses (daan's first production ship stalled on that). The vendored deploy-test accepts a rung declared before its server exists — production with a branch and no path, a branch-only development — instead of failing five checks on the shape the skill prescribes. And it asserts the mail-block exclude on rsync projects. dist/VERSION now tracks the release so make doctor can actually say a project is behind. 0.6.2: make ship leaves from the production branch itself. make finish leaves you on the integration rung, and ship then refused by name ('production deploys from master — you are on develop'), which sent the human to raw git. _ship-branch now runs right after the tty check: clean tree required, checkout of the production branch, fast-forward from origin, refuse on divergence. Two pins in test-makefile.sh. 0.6.0: the promoting verbs survive worktrees. --adopt for projects that predate the plugin. the plugin names no caller; /fleet moved to the fleet repo. one scaffolder driven by templates/stacks.tsv. make push env=<env> and structure.theme_flavour. The single source of truth for Netdust devops: the branch flow, the deploy gate and ledger, and the project/fleet contract. Ships a stack-split Makefile core (mk/wp, statamic, node, generic) that every project vendors rather than copies, so a fix made once reaches every project and `make doctor` names any project that is behind or edited in place. Owns site.yml schema 2 — environments: binds a branch to a server, and nothing else may. Replaces the flow half of netdust-core:dev-stack and both /deploy commands.
